newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on Monday on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.

"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were steady to easier but bond prices were steady to higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months was unchanged from last Friday's yield of 2.95/2.90 percent but one-year closed at a yield of 2.72/2.67 percent compared with last Friday's yield of 2.80/2.75 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 was unchanged from last Friday's close of S$98.53/98.58, September 2001 ended at S$96.35/96.45 against S$96.30/96.40 and June 2003 at S$94.39/94.44 from S$94.35/94.40.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-1/2 3-3/8 percent versus last Friday's 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent.
